companies.name: Nvidia
companies.blurb: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.

companies.name: Apple
companies.blurb: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.

companies.name: Alphabet
companies.blurb: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.blurb: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.blurb: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.blurb: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.blurb: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.

companies.name: Meta
companies.blurb: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.blurb: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

companies.name: Saudi Aramco
companies.blurb: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.blurb: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.

companies.name: Samsung Electronics
companies.blurb: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.

companies.name: Micron
companies.blurb: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.

companies.name: Berkshire Hathaway
companies.sourceLabel: Yahoo Finance · New York Stock Exchange
companies.blurb: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

companies.name: AMD
companies.blurb: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

companies.name: Eli Lilly
companies.sourceLabel: Yahoo Finance · New York Stock Exchange
companies.blurb: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

companies.name: SK Hynix
companies.blurb: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.

companies.name: JPMorgan Chase
companies.sourceLabel: Yahoo Finance · New York Stock Exchange
companies.blurb: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.

companies.name: Walmart
companies.blurb: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

companies.name: ASML
companies.blurb: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
